**Three measured-and-fixed structural bugs** (in `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_vit_tc.cuh`, all bit-identical / parity-gated):

2. **`vittc_dw_biases` ran the full Σ_K (K=278528) redundantly on ALL 132 CTAs** (no nCTA guard) + `clspos` pos-scan iterated all T keeping 1/17. Partitioned bias columns across CTAs; direct stride-kSeq. 580→370 ms.
3. **`vittc_dw_biases` serial-K reduction → warp-parallel** (warp-per-column, 32-lane shuffle tree). grad-assembly 871→7.6 ms. 370→206 ms.

DECODER×GROKADAMW → L3-TC CONVERSION: COMPLETE & VALIDATED (no suppression). This is 1 of the 9-cell campaign; cell #4 of the convertible set.

WHAT WAS DONE — all 3 eager GrokAdamW mechanisms landed faithfully in the bf16 wgmma decoder megakernel (the cell was previously BLOCKED as a "3-mechanism ABI gap"):
- (i) PER-TENSOR layer-wise β1 = β1·(1-γ)^layer + rebased bc1 = 1-β1_i^step. Computed in the kernel P3 work-steal loop where the task id t == the flat named_parameters() layer index (kDecOffsets order == eager enumeration). bc1 MUST be rebased alongside β1 or m_hat=m/bc1 mismatches ~9.6× on the deepest layer. bc2 stays global. This is the mechanism that failed the step-1 state gate (m-rel 0.895 → 4.03e-8 fixed).
- (ii) GLOBAL grad-norm clip to grad_clip (eager clip_grad_norms_device_side is a GLOBAL norm over ALL tensors, NOT per-tensor — verified in helpers.h). New kernel P2.5 phase: deterministic ascending-CTA reduction over the reduced grad → total_norm → clip_coef, broadcast and applied per-element in the tail. grad_out is NOT mutated (the return_grad oracle + eager-side clip both need the unclipped grad). Inert at step 1 (‖g‖₂≈0.72<1), fires ~step 34 — the single-step gate is BLIND to it.
- (iii) ADAPTIVE α = α_init·exp(-κ·signal). The L3 path REPLACES eager opt.step() (where α adaptation lives), so it is threaded host-side: _opt_scalars_from passes optimizer._alpha_for_group(group) for GrokAdamW, and train_grokadamw sets opt._grok_signal/_signal_active on the alpha cadence BEFORE the launch (the ordering trap: a host forward gets train_loss pre-launch since the kernel produces loss only after α is bound).

VALIDATION (B=16384, quiet GPU, against the .so carrying these edits; fresh-rebuild .so smoke-tested as carrying the conversion):
- Single-step state-aware tail_gate grokadamw/decoder: PASS — params rel 5.65e-8, m-state 4.03e-8, v/ema bit-exact, A/A/A deterministic.
- Multi-step parity (80 steps, TOL tightened to 1e-4 so it can fail a dropped mechanism): PASS — kernel tracks clip-ON+α-adapting eager at param 1.2e-7, m 2.03e-7. CONTROL(ii) clip-OFF diverges 2.44e-3; CONTROL(iii) static-α diverges 1.34e-3 — both prove the mechanism is load-bearing AND the kernel matches the faithful (not the dropped-mechanism) reference.
- Race-path verification: train_grokadamw run through the production race entry → wgmma every step, α handed to the kernel adapted off 0.98 at the cadence step.
- No regression: adamw/lion/grokfast/decoder single-step gates + wgmma wiring all still PASS (the P2.5+P3 additions are guarded by `if constexpr (Opt == OptId::GrokAdamW)`).

PER-CELL THROUGHPUT (B=16384): 113.2 ms/step, parity with the shared decoder TC kernel (112.3 ms for adamw/lion/grokfast — the P2.5 global-norm reduce + per-tensor β1 + clip add ~1 ms). 2.85× faster than the scalar megakernel (320 ms). Achieved 0.377 TF/s = 0.25% of the 989 TF/s bf16 peak — the p=97 grokking decoder (422K params, d=128, 2 layers) is intrinsically latency/memory-bound at this scale, not compute-saturated; the TC kernel still wins 2.85× over scalar and grokadamw rides it.
